//: Ratchets for scripts/ci.mjs. Every entry is a thing CI would otherwise fail on, kept green by NAME and by reason. Adding one is a hand edit and shows in a diff; removing one is automatic (`bun run ci -- --update`) because the improvement direction never needs a decision. Same shape and same purpose as scripts/typecheck-baselines.json — see CLAUDE.md Invariant 14.
//exemptPackages: Directories under packages/ (plus the two example apps) with no `test` script. Without this list a package with no tests is indistinguishable from a passing one, which is the failure mode CI is aimed at. Key is the repo-relative directory.

exemptPackages.packages/oracle: A README and a runnable mockup/, nothing else. V2 — deferred until FrontierJS core leaves alpha (FJS-D14, ruled 2026-08-15). The exemption is the answer, not a placeholder: nothing is owed here until then.
exemptPackages.packages/orion: Claimed, not built — basecamp's partner automations app. V2 — deferred until FrontierJS core leaves alpha (FJS-D14, ruled 2026-08-15). Its primary trigger needs a Junction subscriber for litestone onEvent (FJS-010) regardless.
exemptPackages.example: A runnable app, not a package. Its six browser drives need `bun run api` + `bun run web` started by hand and sign in against a login rate limit (10 per 15 min), so they cannot run unattended. Covered by hand per CLAUDE.md § Running things.
exemptPackages.packages/sierra/example: Same — a runnable app whose drives need servers started by hand.

//structure: Architecture-rule exceptions for the `structure` phase, which runs packages/cli/core/checks.js — the same engine `fli check` gives a client app. Keyed by app directory (or `.` for the repo-wide package rules), then by `<rule>:<path-relative-to-that-root>`. A rule is what every app gets on the next release, so an exception is never a loosened rule: it is one named path with a reason, and a stale one is reported.

..package-root-md:packages/css: AGENTS.md. Invariant 17 names four files and this is a fifth, but it is the same KIND of thing as CLAUDE.md — a root-level agent-facing document whose whole value is being findable at the root, under a name other tools have converged on. Ruled 2026-08-14: the four are the standard and a fifth is a question rather than a refusal, so the rule warns; this entry is the answer to the question for this file, which is what an allowance is for now.

packages/basecamp.service-as-system:api/src/services/hub/h: Correct, and does not expire. `/hub/` is the cross-workspace tier — a separate service taking no workspace, behind one `requireSystemAdmin` hook — so reaching every tenant is the whole of what it is for. The request's own client would scope it to the sysadmin's own workspace and answer an empty fleet with a 200.
packages/basecamp.service-as-system:api/src/services/api-k: Correct: it reads what DECIDES the caller's access, which is the class `core/hooks.ts:142` is excluded for. `ApiKey` carries a workspaceId, and this hook reads the key's record to answer whether the key may act at all — through a client already scoped by that answer it could find nothing and refuse every API key as unrecorded. FJS-519's own scope names this class out.
packages/basecamp.service-as-system:api/src/services/jobs/: Correct: `restoreSchedules(app)` runs at BOOT, not inside a call — neither registry survives a restart (`FJS-327`), so this is what re-registers every scheduled job. `$` throws by name outside a call scope, and the read is deliberately fleet-wide: it restores every tenant's schedules.

//generatedIgnored: Files that .gitignore excludes and that a source-extension sweep therefore flags. Each one must be GENERATED — a source file in this list is the `build/`-in-.gitignore incident happening again, where 20 files of Sierra's build pipeline were invisible to a fresh clone.

generatedIgnored.packages/basecamp/web/config/routes.js: Generated by Sierra's route scanner at dev/build time; packages/basecamp/.gitignore:14 excludes it deliberately.

//nonMembers: Directories holding a package.json that the `packages/*` glob cannot see, kept out of the workspace on purpose. Uninstalled means untested and unrunnable (FJS-026), so each one has to say why that is acceptable. A NEW nested package is a note, because the default answer is that it should be a member.

nonMembers.packages/mesa/mesa-bench: A js-framework-benchmark harness, `private: true`, pinning vite 5.4.11 against mesa's own 8.x plus its own remark chain. Making it a member installs a second toolchain for something CI has nothing to assert about. It is run by hand, from its own directory.
nonMembers.packages/orion/mockup/api-engine: Real TypeScript with vitest tests and a typecheck script, inside a package that is otherwise claimed-not-built. Whether orion becomes a workspace member is a V2 question (FJS-D14, ruled 2026-08-15 — deferred until core leaves alpha), not CI's.
nonMembers.packages/oracle/mockup: The entity/pattern recogniser, exported from a Claude artifact and made runnable under the same `mockup/` convention orion and toolbelt use. Deliberately not a member: it is React, d3 and its own vite, and this repo's UI substrate is Mesa — installing it would put a second UI stack on the workspace's import paths for something CI has nothing to assert about. Run by hand from its own directory. V2 (FJS-D14, ruled 2026-08-15).
nonMembers.packages/toolbelt/mockup/datetime: The prototype the `/datetime` kit is being rebuilt from, parked under the same `mockup/` convention orion uses; it moved here with the rest of `packages/datetime-kit`, which is now a subpath of toolbelt rather than a package. Deliberately not a member: `extend()` throws on every call, `add(d, '1 day')` throws, and `src/cron.js` is a stale fork of the fixed one in caravan — installing it would put that on an import path. Reference for the rebuild described in IDEAS/datetime-kit.md, deleted when it lands.

//knownTestFailures: Packages whose own suite exits non-zero today. Listed so that a NEW failure is loud rather than lost in an already-red run. An entry whose suite now passes fails CI until it is removed — that is the ratchet, and `--update` removes it for you.
//knownDeployFailures: Package sources whose deploy branch fails today, by name and reason. The `deploy` phase runs `fli new` → `make:deploy` → `deploy:local` once per source; `npm` grades the PUBLISHED framework and `local` the working tree, and they drift independently. Listed so a NEW failure is loud. An entry whose branch now passes fails CI until it is removed — `bun run ci -- --update` removes it.
//knownUnpublished: Packages the scaffold installs that npm cannot serve yet, by name and reason. The `registry` phase fails on any name not listed here, because a scaffolded app that cannot install is the framework's worst first impression. An entry whose package IS published fails CI until it is removed — that is the ratchet, and it is the day the allowance stops being true.
//removedSnapshots: Committed snapshots that used to exist and deliberately no longer do. The `snapshots` phase expects every snapshot tracked at the base ref to still be here — discovery alone fails open, and a generated artefact that stops existing takes its check with it. Key is the repo-relative path, value is why it is no longer generated.

removedSnapshots.example/web/routes.static.snapshot.md: The prerendered public site moved out of web/ and became its own surface (FJS-D125, FJS-451). Its route table is committed at example/site/routes.snapshot.md, generated by the same command from the new surface root — the snapshot did not stop existing, it moved with the surface it describes.

//knownAdvisories: advisories phase — a package `bun audit` advises against that IS reachable from a published package's runtime dependencies, and is known. Each entry says which VERSION is installed at runtime and why the entry exists, because the advisory names a package and a package can be installed twice. An entry is a record that somebody looked, never a reason not to look again.

knownAdvisories.nanoid: REAL and open — FJS-475's second half. 3.3.17 installed, advisory is <3.3.18: one patch, reached transitively rather than declared, so it moves when whatever pulls it in is updated. happy-dom, the first half, is fixed — every copy is 20.11.6 and no advisory names it.
knownAdvisories.vite: NOT vulnerable at runtime: the copy the closure resolves is 8.2.0 and every advisory here is <=6.4.2. `bun audit` reports a package by NAME, so the old copy installed for a dev tool is reported against the current one. Re-check this entry if the runtime version ever drops.
